newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Somar sees no damaging cold for coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Somar sees no damaging cold for coffee.

text.p: A cold front which brought rains of between 20 and 60 millimeters over the weekend to some Brazilian coffee regions is now in Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states, local meteorologists Somar said Monday.

Temperatures should remain seasonal, with lows in the north of Parana, southwest of Sao Paulo and the Cerrado region of Minas Gerais around 15 and 16 degrees Celsius while in the north of Sao Paulo and south Minas Gerais, minimum temperatures should be around 11 degrees Celsius, Somar said.
A new cold front will reach north Parana and southwest Sao Paulo on June 18, bringing around 20 to 30 millimeters of rain.
The weather system will stretch to more northern coffee regions on June 19, increasing cloud cover but with little rainfall expected.
On June 19 a cold, dry polar air mass will arrive in the south of the country leading to a sharp drop in temperatures in the region.
Temperatures should also fall in the coffee regions but no frosts are forecast in the outlook to June 21, Somar said.
